This is a set and highly allusive opening, which grips hearts directly, shakes them strongly, presses on them, and turns them in every direction. It takes them on a tour of this universe. They see that everywhere there is only Allah. These hearts perceive only Allah. No refuge other than Allah is visible to them. No place of escape other than Allah is seen. They cannot step outside the sphere of Allah's knowledge. There is no place of flight except return to Allah, and wherever they go, the Noble Face of Allah is visible.

In this opening the attributes of lordship (khasa'is al-rububiyyah) are discussed, which in this universe are active, effective, and its Creator. It encompasses everything. It is all-encompassing over everything. It is the All-Knowing of everything. This Being is the originator of this entire universe. It knows the secrets of human hearts. It knows the hidden secrets of hearts, and it is the overseer of this entire universe and all of humanity.

This surah begins by praising the Being of Allah, and this entire universe begins to glorify Allah. Everything in the heavens and the earth is murmuring, and every heart that is open to guidance hears it itself, if no veil lies upon it. There is no need to alter this verse from its apparent meaning, because the word of Allah is just as it is, and we know nothing about this universe; therefore the attributes of this universe are exactly as Allah has told us.

As for "Sabbaha lillahi ... wal-ard" (57:1), its meaning is indeed that "everything that is in the heavens and the earth has glorified Allah," so there is no alteration or change in it. Accordingly, we should be certain that everything in the heavens and the earth has a spirit, and this universal spirit glorifies its Creator. This is the meaning confirmed by authentic narrations and hadiths, and the experiences of some people of inner insight also confirm it, when their hearts are in a state of clarity and illumination, and they become connected with and linked to the reality hidden in things, which lies behind all these things and their forms, namely the universal spirit.

The Qur'an says:

"O mountains, echo with him, and the birds..." (34:10). Thus the mountains and birds were equal for Dawud (David, peace be upon him).

In a hadith, Imam Muslim narrated from Jabir ibn Samurah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "In Makkah there is a stone which used to greet me with salam in the days when I was sent as a prophet, and I still recognize it now." 

Imam Tirmidhi narrated with his chain from Ali ibn Abi Talib: "I was with the Messenger of Allah in Makkah, and we went out to one side of the outskirts of Makkah. Every tree and stone and mountain that came before the Messenger of Allah said, 'As-salamu alayka ya Rasulallah.'"

Imam Bukhari narrated with his chain from Anas ibn Malik that the Messenger of Allah used to deliver sermons beside a palm trunk. When they made a pulpit for him and he stood on it to deliver the sermon, the palm trunk wailed the way a she-camel wails. The Messenger of Allah came down from the pulpit and placed his hand on it, and it fell silent.

The Qur'an's verses are explicit in expressing this reality:

"Do you not see that to Allah prostrate whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of mankind?" (22:18)

Another verse says: "Have you not seen that all who are in the heavens and the earth glorify Allah, and the birds spreading their wings? Each has known its prayer and its glorification" (24:41).

And: "There is not a thing but glorifies Him by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification" (17:44).

Therefore there is no need to interpret these kinds of texts, especially for the purpose of conforming these verses to axioms that are not derived from the Qur'an. The matters of this world must conform to the Qur'an, which was certainly revealed from the Creator, while our self-made principles are changeable and are our own creations.

"Wa huwal-'Azizul-Hakim" (57:1): "And He is the Almighty, the All-Wise." The creatures of the heavens and the earth glorify Him because He is the Almighty and All-Wise, and His wisdom is ultimate wisdom. By His overpowering might He dominates all things, and He has created everything according to His wisdom.

While the general outpouring of this opening verse was still continuing, and we were engaged, along with the whole universe, in a celebration of glorification, a new journey through the higher universe began within the context of the discourse.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 2:

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things.﴾ (75 : 2)

Everything in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah, who is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and in whose ownership He has no partner. This glorification is that of a slave toward his Master, the Truth. This Owner is not a worldly owner. He is the owner of life and death as well. He is the Creator of life and death. He has decreed life for every living thing and death for every creature that dies. Therefore, life and death occur according to His decree.

Life is still a mystery. Its source is none other than Allah. To this day, no one has been able to name any source of life other than Allah, nor has anyone been able to describe how it comes into being. These are great matters. To this day, humans have not even understood the reality of life and death, what they are. The Qur'an says that Allah alone gives life. Allah alone gives life to every living thing. No one has been able to deny this to this day, nor has anyone been able to prove its opposite. In the same way, death is also a mystery, with veils over it. No one knows the nature and essence of death. No one creates death, because one who cannot give life cannot take it away either. All these things are in Allah's absolute ownership. Therefore, He alone gives life to everything in the heavens and the earth, and He alone gives them death.

﴿And He has power over all things.﴾ He has power over everything without limits or restrictions. His will (mashi'ah) is absolute; it is not confined or restricted within any bounds. The connection of His will with everything is constant, and it happens in whatever manner He wills. If human reason places any restriction upon Allah's power, in whatever form, of whatever kind, and in whatever manner, that is false. It is a notion produced by human reason, which is itself limited. The laws of nature (nawamis al-fitrah) that Allah's will has established for this universe are included within His absolute will, since they operate without limits or restrictions. For Allah's will chooses these laws of nature freely, and Allah sometimes even breaks these laws of nature.

The Qur'an has given great importance to this point. Again and again it is affirmed that Allah has power over all things, and that He can even halt the operation of the laws of nature that He Himself created, so that this reality may become clear: that Allah has power over all things, and that there is no trace of anything beyond His power. Allah has promised the people of Paradise that they will abide in Paradise forever, and He has promised the people of Hell that they will abide in Hell. This promise issued as a consequence of Allah's will, yet Allah has kept His own freedom outside the scope of this covenant and has excepted it. Therefore Allah said:

﴿They will abide therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills.﴾ (11:107)

Wherever such a statement occurs, the words "illa ma sha'a Allah" (except as Allah wills) appear, which show that Allah is not bound by His own decisions. It is not permissible to run one's intellect wild in this matter. The Qur'an itself is the true source.

Through this verse, the absolute sovereignty and unrestricted will of Allah over this entire universe has been established. Since He is the Absolute Power, everything glorifies Him.

After filling the cup of this universe to the brim with the unrestricted proof of Allah's sovereignty and His general bounty, another great reality is now brought forward: that apart from Allah, the existence of other things is not real. True existence, reality, and necessary existence belong to Allah alone. He encompasses the whole universe, and He is the All-Knowing of everything.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 57, verse 3:

﴿He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He has knowledge of everything.﴾ He is the First in that nothing exists before Him. He is the Last in that nothing will exist after Him. He is the Manifest, meaning there is nothing above Him, and He is the Hidden, meaning there is nothing below Him.

The words "First" and "Last" encompass the reality of time, and "Manifest" and "Hidden" encompass the reality of space. He exists absolutely in every time and absolutely in every place, and He is not confined to any time or place. According to this conception, He alone is, and there is none other than Him, and our hearts and our perceptions also derive their existence from Him. Therefore, the existence of Allah is the true existence, Allah alone is the Truth, Allah alone is the Reality, and if there is any reality, it is borrowed from Allah. In the whole of this universe, no one else possesses an inherent reality or an inherent existence.

﴿And He has knowledge of everything.﴾ He possesses true and perfect knowledge, because the reality of all things has come from Him, and therefore it lies within His own knowledge. And the knowledge of Allah is such that no one shares in its reality, its nature, or its attributes. No one else possesses such knowledge, however much apparent information the creation may have.

When this reality settles in a heart, it no longer cares for anything other than the Being of Allah. Nothing, not even the human heart and intellect, has any reality or existence except what this Great Reality has bestowed. Everything is illusion and transient. Only Allah remains, and He alone is the true existence.

When a heart firmly establishes this reality within itself, it attains access to that Reality. It reaches a station of extremely lofty tranquility and rest. But as long as it has not attained this station of reaching the Reality, it should continue to reflect upon this verse and strive to reach its meaning and its truth, for the meaning of this verse is itself a great reality.

The people of Sufism grasped this reality, this great truth. They made it their very way of life and drew out many paths from it. Some said that they see Allah in every thing in this universe. Some said that they saw that Allah stands behind every thing. Some said that they saw Allah, and in this universe they see nothing but Allah. If we set aside the variations in wording and the limitations of expression, all these statements point to this same reality. However, the criticism that can be directed at the Sufis is only this: they allowed this conception to overwhelm them to such an extent that they rendered practical life futile. Whereas the balanced approach of Islam was that the minds and hearts of people should absorb this reality, dwell within it and settle in it, while they also fulfil the trust of vicegerency (khilafah) on this earth for which Allah created them, and fulfil all its requirements, the greatest of which is that they establish in this universe the system of life which Allah has sent down in this Qur'an. The purpose is that, in accordance with the conception of this great reality, human beings should spend their lives in this world. This system is in harmony with human nature and with the nature of the universe, just as Allah created it and just as He sent the Qur'an as a guidance.

After placing this great reality in the heart, Allah now says: how did this Great Reality manifest itself in this universe?

He it is Who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and then established Himself upon the Throne. He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. He is with you wherever you may be, and He sees whatever you do. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and all matters are referred back to Him for decision. He causes the night to pass into the day and the day into the night, and He knows the innermost secrets of the hearts.

The reality of the creation of the heavens and the earth, the reality of the establishment upon the Throne, the encompassing and control of all creation, the knowledge of all these things, and the fact that Allah is present with everything wherever it may be; that all affairs return to Allah; that He exercises authority over this entire universe; and that He knows the secrets and thoughts of hearts. All these realities emerge from that great reality mentioned above. However, mentioning these matters again in connection with these cosmic details has an effect upon the heart, and the light of Divine power falls upon it. When this heaven, this earth and this great universe become the focus of human thought, they deeply affect human heart and sight, by their greatness and majesty, by their beauty and order, by their intricate management, by their regular movements, and by their continuity. Furthermore, these created things are creatures like human beings, so the human heart feels a kind of intimacy and love towards them. When the human mind and heart turn towards this great universe and reflect upon its various aspects, strikes are made upon the strings of thought and vision, and from them new intellectual melodies arise. Man listens to them, hears them attentively, and becomes enchanted. What message do these melodies give him? That Allah, who created these, also created him. All these things glorify Allah, and man too glorifies Allah. These things show that we too have received our existence from the Creator of the universe, and so have you. Therefore, in this universe, only that one reality is significant.

What are these six days? Only Allah knows their reality. What is the reality of our days? They are merely the result of the rotation of the earth on its axis before the sun. And this sun and this earth have come into existence after the days of Allah. Therefore, these are not the days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth. So leave this matter to Allah too; when He wills, He will inform us.

As for the Throne of Allah, we believe in it in the manner in which Allah has described it, and we do not know its reality. As for the statement that Allah established Himself upon the Throne, its reality is that it means complete control over this universe, because the Qur'an has clearly stated that Allah does not transition from one state to another; so there was never a time when He was not upon the Throne and later became established upon it. And as for the belief that we have faith in it and do not know its modality, this is a matter which

This picture is very vast, and indeed it is in constant motion, and this motion never stops at any moment. It is not merely an imaginative picture, nor a flash of thought, but an effective suggestive colour that fills every aspect of the human heart and mind; through it, human hearts beat, waves of thought collide with one another, and springs of reflection continue to gush forth. Read carefully:

يعلم ............ فيها (75 : 4) — "He knows what enters into the earth and what comes out of it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it." Every moment countless living and non-living things enter the earth, and likewise every moment countless things come out of it. Rain that falls from the sky, rays that reach here from various stars, meteors that fall, angels that descend, secrets and decrees that come down, and things that ascend into the heavens, those that are seen and those that are not seen, the number of which is known to Allah alone. In short, this brief verse turns thought towards a continuous movement that never ceases, and points to great events whose number is unknown. And human thought clings constantly to this movement, because things are continually entering the earth and things are continually ascending towards the heavens. If a heart constantly turns towards this reality, it can live in the company of Allah; it can wander in His kingdom, while its body remains in its place; it can roam the valleys of this universe, and with great sensitivity and clear, pure thought, in a state of deep fear and God-consciousness, it can wander through the realm of the heavens.

While the reader was still wandering through the valleys of the heavens and the earth with these thoughts, the Qur'an took hold of his hem, saying: take a stroll also in the valley of your own self, when he puts his face into his own collar and thinks about himself. When he wanders in the valleys of his own self, he finds the Lord, the Exalted, present there too. He sees, He knows, and He is very near, nearer than the jugular vein!

وھو معکم ............ بصیر (75 : 4) — "He is with you wherever you are, and He sees whatever you do." This is not a metaphor; it is a reality. Allah is present with everyone, present with everything, present at all times, present in every place. He is aware of every action of His servants and sees it. If someone merely settles this reality in the heart, it is a great reality. It is a reality that, from one aspect, overwhelms a person, and from another aspect grants him hope and love. If this one reality alone settles in a person's heart, it is sufficient to elevate him and purify him. A person turns away from all the worldly interests and self-seekings and becomes Allah's, and then he becomes very cautious in every matter, filled with awe and the fear of Allah, and refrains from falling into any filth, because he feels shame before Allah. Now, a stroll through the valley of the kingdom of the heavens and the earth from another angle. This stroll is of a different kind from the one mentioned earlier.

لہ ملک ............ الامور (75 : 5) — "To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and all matters are referred back to Him for decision." The heavens and the earth were mentioned earlier in connection with creation, and from the standpoint of life and death, and from the angle of divine decree and destiny. Here, from the angle that their decisions return to Allah, the King. When Allah is the Owner, then the making of decisions is also within His authority.

When this consciousness becomes firm in a person, then in every matter he sees the good pleasure of Allah. At the beginning and at the end of his actions he sees what Allah's will is. This consciousness makes a person independent of other than Allah, makes him dependent on Allah in every matter, and guides him on the path of Allah everywhere, in solitude and in society. His movement and rest, his counsel and his thinking are all under Allah's supervision, and he is certain that there is no place to flee and no refuge except Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 6:

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He knows what is within the breasts.﴾ The entering of the night into the day and the entering of the day into the night is a continuous movement, but it is an extremely subtle movement, which apparently appears calm. Whether its meaning is that the night and day keep growing and shrinking, so that a part of the night is given to the day or a part of the day is shortened and given to the night, or that at the times of sunrise and sunset they overlap one another, in any case it is a continuous and subtle movement. And there is a movement within hearts too. It is the movement of thought, and it occurs in the heart at all times. Everything is within the knowledge of Allah. The human consciousness that everything is in the hand of Allah, who causes the night to enter into the day and the day to enter into the night, is an extremely subtle consciousness, and this consciousness that Allah knows even the most subtle and hidden thoughts of hearts is a great thing!

This first paragraph of the surah sharpens human perception to such a degree that it is now ready to receive guidance. Therefore, the Islamic community is now commanded: believe, and display spending in the way of Allah at the appropriate time. This guidance is given in circumstances in which the inner self of a person, and all the paths leading to his heart, have their doors open; his consciousness is awake and he is eager to listen. Accordingly, in such a state this call comes. But it also comes with arguments of great impact and warnings that shake one awake.

Here Allah addresses the hearts that He Himself created. Allah alone knows the pathways by which speech enters those hearts, for He is well aware of their conditions. Allah knows even the most hidden thoughts. Allah knows how faith settles into hearts, how the heart is purified of non-faith impurities, and how this faith then grows in practical life like a great tree, and how a person advances in spending in the way of Allah and sacrifices even his life in the path of Allah. This is a station far beyond human power, and reaching it requires a great struggle. For this reason Allah gives His creation this kind of argument, impact and guidance for their training. He places before them the realities of the whole universe so that the human being may be moved by them and weigh and measure all things on the scale of Allah. Allah arranges this for the training of man again and again and at every step.

And it is not merely that a plain command is issued that the believers should act upon the following matters. The Qur'an does not issue such a dry circular, nor does it enact a dry law, but everywhere it gives convincing arguments. At every moment it plays upon the strings of human thought. The Qur'anic style and method of training human beings are worthy of which the callers to the Islamic revolution should reflect deeply, understand it, and act upon it. The effective arguments and indications given at the beginning of this surah left deep impressions on hearts. On reading them, the hardest hearts melt and even the most sleepy and intoxicated consciousness awakens. But the Qur'an continues to shake them repeatedly in the second paragraph as well, and its allusions and exhortations continue. Directives and injunctions also continue, and alongside them arguments and indications continue.

"Believe in Allah and His Messenger, and spend of that over which He has made you successors (khulafa'). (57:7)"

The address in this verse is to Muslims, indeed to the very earliest believers of the first age. Yet they too are told: believe in Allah and in the Messenger of Allah. The meaning is: create true faith within your hearts. This is a profound guidance and a deep point, because the call is toward spending in the way of Allah, but before it there is the indication that you must produce genuine faith within your hearts. And after the command to spend, there is again an indication and guidance that what you are spending is not from your own wealth; it is Allah's wealth, which He has entrusted to you under your stewardship and succession. For you have just been told that—

"To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. (57:5)" It is Allah who has given human beings a limited succession and vicegerency on this earth. He is the One who gives life and causes death. Thus He has made you successors on the earth generation after generation.

The fundamental principles stated at the beginning of the surah are linked with these guidances. And now all these concepts together persuade the believers that the Owner who has made you successors on this earth and over its treasures has given you everything; tell me, He is now asking you for a portion of His own wealth. What do you think? Will you give something to Allah? Behold, Allah is the Giver, and there is no shortage in His treasures. Why do you hold back your hand? It all belongs to Him!

Yet the matter does not end merely with arguments, persuasion, and admonition, and with mere hope. After this comes an effective address: that for this spending you will receive a very great reward, and His grace and bounty will also be upon you.

"Those among you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward. (57:7)" Now who could abandon the bond of faith and remain behind? Who could hold back from spending, and who could deprive himself of this grace and bounty?

But the matter does not end even here. After these stirrings, arguments, guidances and indications, people are now invited to consider the time as well, to feel the gravity of the circumstances, and by presenting the conditions of that time it is said what the demand of the moment is.

ومالکم ............ رحیم (9) (75 : 8۔ 9)

﴿What is the matter with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord, and he has already taken a covenant from you, if you are indeed believers? It is He who sends down to His servant clear verses, that He may bring you out of darkness into light. And indeed Allah is to you Most Kind and Merciful.﴾

Why is there an obstacle in the way of faith? They have already believed; what is required here is the right to believe. Moreover, the call comes from the Messenger himself, at whose hand you have already pledged allegiance and made a firm promise. And then, from the heavens, clear verses are descending in continuous, torrential rain. These verses are bringing you out of darkness, doubt and confusion. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 10:

ومالکم ................ والارض (75 : 01) "And what is [the matter] with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, while to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth?" This repeats the truth that was stated earlier.

لہ ملک ................ الامور "To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned [for decision]." The inheritance of Allah, His sovereignty and His kingship, are His; and to whom sovereignty belongs, the decisions also belong to Him, and whatever authority He has granted to them will all soon return to Him. Therefore, when Allah is calling you to spend, and this wealth is His, and it is He who has granted you the authority to dispose of it, and it will return to Him, then there remains no justification for stinginess and miserliness. This address contains only this truth.

A handful of the foremost ones (al-sabiqun al-awwalun) spent in the way of Allah whatever was within their means. These were the pure people among the Muhajirun and the Ansar, and they spent in the most difficult of times. In the period of extreme hardship they gave financial sacrifice, and they spent at a time when Islam was surrounded by dangers from every side. In the period before the conquest of Makkah or Hudaybiyyah, the friends and helpers of Islam were few, and the enemies were many. In that period, what these people spent, they had no worldly hope or greed for it. Nor did they spend it to be seen by anyone. All this spending was based on the impulse of goodness, the goodness which they had adopted. They were spending for that ideology which they had adopted by leaving all worldly interests. They spent heaps of wealth. Some spent an amount equal to what the foremost ones had spent before the conquest. Verses of the Qur'an were revealed concerning this, and they explicitly stated that in terms of quantity your spending may equal or even exceed theirs, but in the scale of Allah the spending of the foremost ones is preferable, because of the difference in the faith-driven impulse with which they spent.

لا یستوی ................ وقتلوا (75 : 01) "Those among you who spend and fight after the conquest can never be equal to those who spent and fought before it. Their rank is greater than those who spent and fought afterwards." One person is he who spends and fights at a time when the ideology is attacked from every side, its believers and friends are few, and there is not even a trace of benefit: there is no authority and no conveniences. Another person spends and fights when the way of life is at peace, its supporters are many, and victory, dominance, conquest and interests are expected; between the two there is a great difference. The first person is wholly attached to Allah alone; he is sincere, and there is no room for doubt in his sincerity. He has deep reliance on Allah and tranquility in Allah alone. This person is far from apparent means and worldly interests. Only his belief inspires him to that goodness and virtue, whereas the second person who does good has other motives besides his ideology that move him to that virtue, even if his intention is clear, other factors are still considered.

Imam Ahmad narrated: from Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik, from Zuhayr, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas, who said: some words were exchanged between Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. Khalid said to Abd al-Rahman: "You treat us with harshness because you embraced Islam some days before us." This matter was reported to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "Leave my companions alone. By Him in whose hand my soul is, even if you were to spend gold equal to Mount Uhud (or he said, equal to the mountains), you would not reach their deeds..." It is in Sahih [al-Bukhari and Muslim]:

"لا تسبوا اصحابی فوالذی نفسی بیدہ لو انفق احدکم مثل احد ذھبا ما بلغ مد احدھم او نصیفہ" ("Do not revile my companions. By Him in whose hand my soul is, if one of you were to spend gold equal to Uhud, he would not reach the mudd of one of them, nor even half of it") (1). (A mudd is a measure of roughly two kilograms.) It appears that in this hadith "my companions" has a specific meaning. Regarding them the Prophet (ﷺ) gave a severe warning. These people are in reality the foremost ones. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say to the companions and believers around him: "Leave my companions for me," meaning the special companionship. Once, regarding Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, he said: "Leave my companion for me."

But those who came later were also not disappointed. There is a lofty station for all, and a good promise.

وکلا وعد ................ الحسنی (75 : 01) "And Allah has promised good to both." Although there was a difference in rank between them, they were all good and honoured.

But this difference, and the promise of a good reward to all, are all subject to Allah's knowledge; Allah is well aware of the circumstances of all. It is Allah who knows what motive lay behind those deeds. Only Allah possesses true knowledge.

واللہ ............ خبیر (75 : 01) "And Allah is Aware of what you do."

This is such a touch and such a pinch by which hearts awaken: the outward deeds are in their place and the judgments of the world are in their place, but Allah's judgments will be based on Allah's knowledge. Beware: there the weighing will be by Allah's scales.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, *Fi Zilal al-Quran* (Urdu translation), on Surah 57, verses 11–12:**

﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward?﴾ [57:11] (75: 11 to 51)

"Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan (*qard hasan*, a sincere, voluntary gift given for Allah's sake), so that He may multiply it many times over for him and give him an excellent reward? On the day when you see the believing men and women, their light running before them and on their right side. (It will be said to them,) 'Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which you will abide forever. That is the great success.' On that day the hypocrite men and women will say to the believers, 'Look upon us, so that we may benefit from your light.' But it will be said, 'Go back and seek light elsewhere.' Then a wall will be set up between them, with a gate in it. Inside the gate will be mercy, and outside it will be punishment. They will call out to the believers, 'Were we not with you?' The believers will reply, 'Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, you waited (for misfortune), you doubted, and false hopes deceived you until the command of Allah came. And the great deceiver (Satan) deceived you concerning Allah. So today no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who openly disbelieved. Your abode is the Fire; it is your protector, and it is an evil destination.'"

This is a powerful call from the Lord of Majesty, a forceful and effective signal, which Allah addresses to His needy and dependent servants.

﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan?﴾ [57:11] The purpose of this is that the mere idea that a Muslim is poor and always in need before Allah, and that the Lord of Majesty is asking him for a loan, is enough to make him spend freely in the way of Allah. People are accustomed to investing their capital in profitable enterprises. Since they are poor, and a loan given to Allah is safe and its repayment is certain, and since it is also an honour for them to lend to Allah, there is no reason why people should not invest in this enterprise. Generally, people invest money in profitable business, and Allah repays it many times over. Therefore there is no reason for people not to invest in this trade.

Allah does not merely take people to good feelings; He promises that He will multiply such a goodly loan for them many times over, on the condition that it is a goodly loan given solely for Allah's sake. Along with this multiplication, they will also receive a further reward from Allah.

﴿So that He may multiply it for him and he will have a noble reward.﴾ [57:11] This reward is depicted through a scene from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. On that day this reward will be given, and it will be a very precious reward.

This scene is a completely new scene among the scenes of the Qur'an. It is depicted in such a way that, full of movement and dialogue, it becomes a living scene. When we read the Qur'an today, the whole picture comes before our eyes. We see the believing men and women walking in intense darkness, but in front of them and to their right we see a subtle light and radiance. This light is the light of faith of those people of belief, and it is radiating from their faces. From the bodies of these believing men and women this light is shining, and by its illumination they are moving forward in the darkness of that day. It is the same light that Allah gave them in the darknesses of *jahiliyyah* (the pre-Islamic age of ignorance), and in its light they used to walk. Now this light has overcome their earthly bodies through their spirits. It is also possible that this light is shining from the earthly parts of their bodies, since modern scientific research is also moving in this direction, that matter is made of atoms and that the atom is in reality light and "rays." Thus this light will truly be real light.

Now, in this scene, the believing men and women are given congratulations.

﴿Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow, in which you will abide forever. That is the great success.﴾ [57:12]

But the scene of congratulations does not end here. From the other side, a group of hypocrite men and women is also coming, stumbling and falling. They are bewildered and in a state of helplessness. These people cling to the believing men and women and say...

﴿On that Day the hypocrite men and the hypocrite women will say to those who believed: "Look upon us, that we may borrow some of your light."﴾ The group of believing men and believing women, wherever it turns, sees nothing but light, pure and transparent. But how can the group of hypocrite men and hypocrite women benefit from that light, when they have spent their whole lives in the darkness of ignorance? At this moment an unknown voice calls out:

﴿It will be said: "Turn back, and seek a light."﴾ It appears that this voice will be raised for their humiliation and as a mockery of them, and that the reminder it is meant to convey is this: in the world you used to prepare your hypocritical policies in the darkness of the night. So go back to the world and seek your light there. Go back, for this light comes from the world; it is obtained through deeds done in the world. Today you are in the abode of recompense; what are you seeking here?

At this stage, suddenly, a separation is made between the group of believing men and believing women and the group of hypocrite men and hypocrite women, because this is the Day of Separation. In the world these people had slipped into the ranks of the Muslims.

﴿So a wall will be set up between them, with a gate in it. Within it there will be mercy, and without it, before it, there will be torment.﴾ This will be a wall through which nothing will be visible, but voices will be heard. Now the group of hypocrites will call out to the believers.

They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" They will say, "Yes, but you led yourselves into temptation, waited and doubted, and were deceived by false hopes until the command of Allah came; and the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah."

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given. Here is the faithful translation:

They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?" Now why are you separating from us? In the world we lived together in one place, on one level, and here too we have been raised together in one place with you.

They will say, "Yes," meaning: the matter is indeed so.

"But you led yourselves into temptation," meaning: you broke yourselves away from guidance.

"And you waited (for opportunity)," meaning: you practiced opportunism. You did not resolve, with determination, to take up the path of truth in a decisive manner.

"And you doubted," meaning: you remained in doubt. You were not given the treasure of certainty by which you would have plunged into the fire of Nimrod.

"And false hopes deceived you," meaning: false expectations kept deceiving you. You thought that success lay in wavering, hypocrisy, and holding the staff by both ends.

"Until the command of Allah came," meaning: until the decision of Allah arrived.

"And the great deceiver deceived you concerning Allah," meaning: until the end, that great deceiver kept deceiving you about the matter of Allah. This was Satan: he kept offering you new greeds and settling you in a world of desires. Now the believers remind them of this and pronounce the verdict, as though the decision now lies in their hands.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 15:

Fa-al-yawma ... al-masir (75:51): "So today no ransom will be accepted from you, nor from those who openly disbelieved. Your abode is the Fire; it is your protector, and what an evil destination it is."

This is probably an announcement from the court of the Almighty Sovereign, a response from Allah.

If we look at the artistic harmony of this scene, there is a special wisdom in the choice of light. This passage concerns the group of hypocrite men and hypocrite women, and the true character of the hypocrites is that they conceal their inner selves and display something other than what is hidden in their hearts. They always carry out their hypocrisy in darkness. Darkness conceals, and light reveals. Thus the two characters are also opposites: faith and hypocrisy, and the two colours are also opposites: light and darkness. From these two things the scene becomes extremely beautiful. Faith is shown as bright, and hypocrisy as dark. The believers travel in light, while the hypocrites stumble about in darkness. The meanings have also been expressed through the lights of the scene. (Mushahid al-Qiyamah)

Who is there who, on that day, would not seek light and yearn for it? Who is there who would still shy away from spending in the way of Allah after this? Despite such effective arguments, interests and a good end... This is the Qur'an's method of teaching and training. The Qur'an trains the believers with great continuity and steadfastness, and like a skilled and all-knowing, all-aware teacher, it so wisely imprints guidance and lessons upon the minds of its students that they become ready for immediate action.

After this comes the second session, in which there is likewise a continuous call, and in the same manner and style the Muslim community is urged to act.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 16:

Alam ya'ni ... taʿqilun

This is a most impactful call from the Lord, the Most Generous and Most Merciful: by now your hearts should have been filled with the fear of Allah and with humility and submission. Allah's great favour has already been bestowed upon you. Among you there is a Messenger who is calling you to faith. Clear signs have been revealed upon this Messenger so that he may bring you out of darkness into light. And He has also shown you signs in this universe and in your own creation.

This is a rebuke that is full of love. It contains sympathetic kindness. It stirs enthusiasm and awakens awareness that Allah is supremely exalted. Remember Him with humility and submission, and receive the truth that comes from Allah with utmost honour, respect, obedience and surrender. However, the question clearly implies that your pace is slow.

Alam ya'ni ... min al-haqq (57:16). "Has not the time come for those who believe that their hearts should melt at the remembrance of Allah and bow before the truth that He has sent down?"

Along with this stirring and this reproach for slowness, they are also warned of the evil consequence of not responding and of dragging their feet: when hearts are not continually cleansed, they become rusted and hardness enters them. This happens when they become heedless of the remembrance of Allah and forget to bow before the truth:

Wa la yakunu ... fasiqun (57:16). "And let them not be like those who were given the Scripture before, but a long period passed over them and their hearts became hardened, and many of them are now defiant transgressors."

When hearts become hard, the next stage is wickedness and immorality (fisq and fujur).

The human heart changes very quickly, and a human being forgets very quickly. When it is pure, clear and bright, waves of light rise from it and it shines like a pearl. But when much time passes over it, or reminder and training cease, it becomes hard and rusted. Therefore it constantly needs reminder and training so that humility and submission arise within it. It should be knocked upon again and again so that it remains soft and clean, and one should always remain alert lest it become hard-hearted and dull.

But if a heart has grown dim, turned into stone, become hard and dull, there is no need for despair. It can be brought to life anew, life can enter it anew, and it can bow again before Allah. Allah is the Possessor of power; He revives the dead earth anew. A dead land, within moments, becomes full of life and fresh, lush and green, and begins to yield fruits and produce. The same is the condition of hearts.

"Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death" ﴿Know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death.﴾ And in the Qur'an there is that which revives hearts after their death. Within it is the material that nourishes, that gives drink, and that warms.

﴿We have made the signs clear to you, that perhaps you may use your reason.﴾ (75 : 71)

After this life-giving prod, after this indirect reproach, and after this warning, the call to spend in the way of Allah (infaq fi sabilillah) is made again.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 18:

Those who give charity, men and women, and who lend to Allah a goodly loan, will have it multiplied for them, and they will have a generous reward. They do not display their superiority over those who receive their charity, and in this transaction they are not the parties concerned; their dealing is with Allah. What could be a loftier or more exalted awareness than that the giver of charity thinks he is lending to the One who is self-sufficient and worthy of all praise? He is dealing with the Master of this universe, and what he spends will be returned to him many times over, and after multiplying it manifold, a noble reward will also be given.

The station of the siddiqin (the truthful, those who are foremost in sincere faith) is a very elevated station, and the Prophetic traditions explain it at length. Although this station is very lofty, the opportunities to attain it are open to everyone; it is not confined to a few individuals or to a particular class. Whoever brings forth sound faith in Allah and His Messenger and aspires to this lofty station can attain it; there is no limit to the bounty of Allah.

﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers, they are the siddiqun in the sight of their Lord﴾ (57:19). This is the distinguishing feature of this religion: it is an open path for all of mankind. It is a lofty horizon toward which everyone's gaze should be fixed. Here no one has a monopoly, and these ranks are not granted to any specific people. In Islam, a person can reach the highest degrees through action. This is a religion in which there is no room for any class that holds an inherent, hereditary superiority.

Imam Malik, in his book al-Muwatta, narrates from Safwan ibn Sulaym, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: The people of Paradise will see those in the lofty chambers, as they are high up, just as you see a bright star in the eastern or western horizon, because of the great difference in their ranks. The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) asked: O Messenger of Allah, would these be the stations of the prophets, which no one else can reach? He said: Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, they will be men who believed in Allah and affirmed the messengers. This is the level of faith in its first stage and of sacrifice for the religion of Allah? That comes later.

﴿And the martyrs, for them is their reward and their light﴾ (57:19). The matter of martyrs is mentioned repeatedly in the Qur'an, and the Prophetic traditions about them are also widely transmitted. They are the guardians of this religion, and no religion can survive without vigilance. A religion can never be established in any land without jihad. The purpose of jihad is that belief be protected, that the path be open for the call to Islam, and that the people of religion and of the Shariah be safeguarded from corruption. For this reason, only the martyrs in the way of Allah are the martyrs of this lofty station; they will be near their Lord, and they will be with their Lord. ʿInda rabbihim is their honour.

It is related in the Sahihayn that the souls of martyrs are in the form of green birds in Paradise, and they feed wherever they wish. Afterwards they return and rest in those lamps. Allah will appear to them and say: What do you desire? They will say: We desire that we be returned to the world and fight again in Your way as we fought the first time. Then Allah will say: I have decided that they will not be returned to the world.

He will wish to be returned to the world and to be killed in the way of Allah ten times, because he will have seen the honour of the martyrs.

Upon hearing these matters, life held no importance for the Muslims of the first era. Those Muslims who learned the station of martyrdom...

Imam Malik narrates from Yahya ibn Sa'id that once the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was urging people to jihad, and he was mentioning Paradise. A man from the Ansar was listening, and he had some date-kernels in his hand that he was eating. He said: "I am greedy for this world, if I sit and keep eating these dates until I finish them." He threw the dates away, took up his sword, and attacked the disbelievers until he was killed. It is reported that this man's name was ʿUmayr ibn al-Hammam (may Allah be pleased with him).

Since this is the station of the siddiqin and this is the station of the martyrs, the station of the disbelievers and deniers is also described.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 19:

"And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, they are the companions of the Hellfire" (75:91 [as quoted in the commentary]). Who could forsake this honour and this rank, and risk being counted among the people of Hell?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 20:

اعلموا ................ متاع الغرور (75 : 02) "Know that the life of this world is nothing but play and amusement, outward show and boasting among yourselves, and competing with one another in wealth and children. Its example is like rain whose vegetation pleases the tillers; then it dries up and you see it turning yellow; then it becomes chaff. In the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure. The life of this world is nothing but the delusion of an illusory enjoyment."

Translating this passage: The life of this world, when measured by worldly standards, appears to outward eyes as a great matter and a very big problem. But if this world is viewed from the perspective of the whole universe and weighed by the scale of the Hereafter, it is a very insignificant thing. Here the Holy Qur'an tells us that this world, in comparison to the Hereafter, is a plaything of children, because the real world is the Hereafter, to which people must go at the end of this world.

Play, spectacle, adornment, boasting, and seeking abundance in everything: behind all the intense struggle and all the occupations of the world, there is nothing but this. The Qur'an presents this whole game of the world in the form of a scene, in its own distinctive style.

كمثل ................ نباته (75 : 02) "Its example is like rain whose vegetation pleases the tillers." Here "kuffar" means the tillers. The lexical meaning of kufr is to conceal. Linguistically, a farmer is called a kafir because he hides the seed in the earth. But here there is also an allusion to kufr, that he rejoices in worldly life.

ثم ................ مصفرا (75 : 02) "Then the crop ripens and you see it turn yellow," and becomes ready to be cut, because this greenness has an appointed time, and very soon it reaches the time of harvest.

ثم ............ حطاما (75 : 02) "Then it becomes chaff." Now on the screen this movement and running about ends. With the scene of the harvest being cut, the scene of worldly life also ends.

As for the Hereafter, its status is entirely different. Its status is that it should be kept in mind, given importance, and preparation should be made with it in view.

وفى الاخرة ................ ورضوان (75 : 02) "In the Hereafter there is severe punishment, and forgiveness from Allah and His good pleasure." The Hereafter does not pass in a few moments the way this world passes in a few moments. It is not like a grain that sprouts and then becomes chaff and is finished. Rather, in the Hereafter there is reckoning and accounting, and then eternity. Therefore its outcome should be this.

ومالحيوة ................ الغرور (75 : 02) "The life of this world is nothing but the delusion of an illusory enjoyment." The provisions of this life have no intrinsic reality. It is a deception. It keeps a person occupied in play and amusement, and his life ultimately falls prey to deception.

If a person sets out to seek the truth seriously, this life is indeed a deception. But the sense in which Islam and the Qur'an have called worldly life "the delusion of enjoyment" needs to be well understood. The purpose of the Qur'an is not that a person become detached from worldly affairs and renounce the world. Nor does Islam teach that one should take no interest in the building and progress of the world, or neglect the responsibility that man must discharge as the vicegerent of Allah. Rather, Islam wishes that human consciousness about the value and reality of the world be corrected, and that man be told what the true worth of this world is: that the world is a transient place, a temporary abode that every person must leave behind. Its attraction and importance should be proportionate to this. The people to whom this Surah was addressed were the first believers, and they had certain obligations of faith; it was necessary to correct their conception and consciousness of the world so that they could fulfil their duties of faith. Every believer needs this perspective in relation to his creed and worldview. If the believer is to establish his creed and way of life here, he must purify his heart of attachment to this world.

Thus Islam gives them a new field for progress and advancement. It is the true field of progress and advancement, a goal related to their final destiny, and related to the eternal world and the abode of the Hereafter.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 57, verse 21:

"Hasten (sabiqu) to forgiveness from your Lord and to a Paradise whose breadth is like the breadth of heaven and earth, prepared for those who believe in Allah and His messengers. That is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of mighty grace." (57:21)

This race is not in gathering the playthings of amusement, nor in gathering much wealth. It is the race of those who have cast off from their necks the yoke of slavery to this world, and have left the field of play and amusement to children. Their gaze is fixed on a lofty horizon, and their goal lies a little beyond this world.

"Paradise whose breadth is like the breadth of heaven and earth" (57:21): a Paradise whose width and extent are like the heavens and the earth.

Some exegetes, at a time when our knowledge of the vastness of this universe was limited, adopted the view that this verse means great vastness in a figurative sense. In the same way, they also interpreted some prophetic traditions figuratively. Likewise, the hadith which states that the people of Paradise will see the people of the lofty chambers as clearly as a bright star visible on the horizon, in the east or in the west, was also understood by commentators as referring to great height. But today, the vastness of this universe that the very small telescopes made by humans reveal to us is astonishing and dizzying. The traditions about the vastness of Paradise, and those traditions in which the lofty chambers appear like stars on the horizon, show realities that are very close to reason, indeed very close to observation, and there is no need to interpret the Quranic verses or the traditions concerning the vastness of Paradise figuratively.

Anyone who intends it can reach that vast and wide kingdom of Paradise. Every person can strive forward and attain it, but its earnest-money (bayana) is faith in Allah and His messengers.

"That is the grace of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the Lord of mighty grace" (57:21).

The grace of Allah is boundless and without reckoning, and there is no restriction upon it. This grace is open to all those who have an interest in it. Therefore, people should race ahead of one another in attaining this grace of Allah, not within this narrow-bounded earth alone, but within the boundless universe of Allah.

It is the duty of an ideological person to deal with this great universe, and not to confine his self, his outlook, his imagination, his priorities and his consciousness within this narrow and limited world. Unless ideological people broaden their outlook, they will not be able to render any worthwhile service to the Islamic ideology of life, because the Islamic ideology of life clashes with people's meanness, humiliations and selfishness. It also clashes with people's misguidance and crookedness.

Then, a false power always confronts the ideological person, and since it controls a portion of the earth, only the one whose concern is with a great universe, and who holds a wider outlook than this earth, can stand against it. And he holds aims and objectives in the wider world beyond this transient life, namely the pleasure of Allah.

The aims and standards of this earth can never be lofty aims and objectives for an ideological person. Their importance for a believer is just as much as the status of the earth in comparison with the universe. This entire earth is neither eternal nor everlasting. There is no comparison at all between the earth and the universe of Allah: the earth is small and its aims are very small.

Thus the outlook of a believer is very wide and very lofty, even though the earth may appear very beautiful, long and broad. The ideological person deals with the reality that is boundless, while limits and restrictions apply to the earth; he confronts the reality that exists eternally and everlastingly. And this great reality lies in the vast field of the Hereafter. Even if there is some increase or decrease in the lowly values of this world, it has no effect on the values of faith. Those whose aim is the attainment of these lofty values are free-willed servants of Allah and are liberated from the limited values of this world.

Now comes the fourth pinch. It makes one feel deeply that whatever befalls a person in this world is from Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 22:

ما اصاب .................... الحمید (42) (75 : 22 تا 42)

"No calamity befalls the earth or yourselves but that it is in a Record (Kitab) before We bring it into being. Indeed that is easy for Allah. [This is] so that you do not despair over what has escaped you and do not exult over what He has given you. And Allah does not like everyone self-deluding and boastful, who are stingy and enjoin stinginess upon the people. And whoever turns away – indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy."

Every event that occurs in this universe has already been recorded by Allah, in all its details, before it happened, and it is determined and measured within the plan and design of this universe. There is no room in it for mere chance or coincidence. Before the creation of this entire universe, Allah, through His complete and all-encompassing knowledge, has done this, and has recorded everything in great detail; this was within Allah's knowledge. In Allah's knowledge there is no past, present and future. These boundaries and distances of time and space do not restrict Allah's knowledge. It is we who, through our limited knowledge, see these things confined within time and space. We cannot see them without these limits and restrictions. Then we cannot perceive the Absolute Reality. Yes, at times the perceptive power of human beings acquires a kind of brightness, at the moment when our soul becomes connected with the Absolute Reality, and we can know the reality of things in the usual manner, that is, through the senses. As for Allah, who is the Absolute Reality, He knows every thing in this universe without limits and restrictions. This universe and the events within it, from their beginning to their end, are in Allah's knowledge. This knowledge is absolute and without limits or restrictions. And in Allah's plan every thing and event has a place which is known to Allah. Therefore every event, whether a person considers it good or evil, occurs on the earth, and what happens in human lives is recorded in the Book of Allah.

﴿Indeed that is easy for Allah.﴾ (57:22)

What is the benefit of this? The benefit of this truth is that a person, who experiences both joy and worry over the events of this world, should regard them as coming from Allah, and live in this world with peace and tranquility. If they see disagreeable things, they should not consume themselves with regret, and if they see events that bring joy, they should not go beyond themselves, and they should understand, as is the reality, that all of this is from Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verses 23–24:

So that you do not grieve over what escapes you, and do not exult over what He has given you (57:23). ﴿So that you do not grieve over what has escaped you, nor exult over what He has given you.﴾ (Qur'an 57:23)

Therefore, when one's outlook becomes universal, and one connects one's affairs with the vast universe, and thinks in terms of eternity and infinity, and regards whatever befalls one as a decree from the Book of Destiny, the human soul expands. The person becomes great, becomes steadfast, and resolutely faces events and incidents, and as he passes through the movement of the universe, the human soul traverses whatever comes to it with success.

When a person separates himself from this great universe, he is seized by anxiety and distress over the events that befall him. He displays great shallowness. But when a person holds this belief, and it is firmly settled in his mind, that he and these events and collisions are of one piece, just as in a great universe particles both collide with one another and fulfil their purpose, and work according to a vast design, and this design has been prepared from eternity, and all these individuals are necessarily bound up with one another, then he attains the tranquillity that what has gone wrong had to go wrong. Thus he is not distressed at deprivation, nor does he go beyond himself when something is received.

But the station in which a servant entrusts himself wholly to God is granted to only a few people. As for all Muslims, this belief delivers them from the bitterness of afflictions and calamities, and in this way restrains them from exulting in prosperity. In both conditions a believer is of balanced temperament. Ikrimah (may Allah have mercy on him) said well:

"Every person is both joyful and sorrowful; turn joy into gratitude and sorrow into patience."

This is Islam's moderate standpoint.

﴿Allah does not love anyone who is arrogant and boastful, who are stingy and urge others to stinginess.﴾ (Qur'an 57:23–24)

What is the connection between the themes of destiny, boasting and stinginess? It is this: one who believes that whatever befalls him comes from Allah never displays pride, arrogance or boasting, nor does he diminish his generosity, nor is he stingy, nor does he invite others to stinginess. But those who have no awareness of this reality and do not believe in it think that what they have acquired is their own accomplishment; therefore they boast and act with arrogance, and afterwards they do not spend in the paths of goodness, for such a person reasons that if these poor people were capable, they too would have earned.

﴿And whoever turns away—indeed Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ (Qur'an 57:24) Whoever spends, prepares provision for the Hereafter for himself, and whoever obeys Allah's command, good will be his. Allah says that He is not in need of His needy servants. He is praiseworthy in His own essence and self-sufficient; He has no need of people's praise or support.

Now comes the final paragraph of the surah. It briefly mentions a line of messengers in this world: the history of the Islamic worldview from Nuh (peace be upon him) onward, what purpose it had in this world, and finally Isa (peace be upon him), the revelation of the Injil, and the condition of the community of Isa.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 25:

The reality of prophethood is one. The message of all the prophets was one, which the Messengers brought in different eras. Many Messengers were given miracles, and some Messengers were given scriptures, as the Quran says:

﴿And We sent down with them the Book﴾ (57:25 as cited, 75:52 in the source) "We sent down with them the Book." The Messengers were one, the Book was one, and the call was one; therefore the nature of prophethood is one.

What is the Mizan (the Balance) along with the Book? Every Prophet came so that humanity would be given a balance on which they could weigh their good and evil, and by which they could correct their deeds. Deeds, events and people are to be weighed on this balance. By it, people's lives are set right, the direction of their various desires is set right, and balance is created among their different temperaments, and conflicting interests are decided. It is a balance that favours no one; it is the balance of truth, which does not oppress anyone; it is the balance of Allah, who is the Lord of all.

This Mizan which Allah sent down upon the Messengers is, for humanity, a guarantee against all the imbalances into which humanity has been afflicted: all the agitations, all the disorder, and all the storms that humanity repeatedly faces. Where clashes of desires take place, where storms of emotions rise, where the dust of stubbornness and enmity takes the form of whirlwinds, where people become Pharaohs. It was necessary that this Mizan be such that everyone bows before it, and that under this Mizan everyone receives justice and equity.

﴿That mankind may uphold justice﴾ (57:25) "That people may establish justice." In short, without this balance, which conforms to the system of life and the system of law prescribed by Allah, people can never attain justice and equity. Even if people at some time attain justice, they cannot maintain it; due to their desires and their ignorance, the balance of justice quickly slips from their hands.

﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ (57:25) "And We sent down iron in which is great might and benefits for people. This is said so that it may be known who helps Allah and His Messengers in the unseen. Indeed Allah is Strong and Mighty." The expression of sending down iron from the heavens is like that found in other places.

"And He sent down for you eight pairs of cattle" (39:6). In both places the purpose is that Allah created things for this purpose; as if their creation is according to the decree of Allah. Then, in keeping with the atmosphere of the verse and for the sake of harmony, the root "to send down" has been used here as well, since earlier there was mention of the sending down of the Book and the sending down of the Balance. Thus it is said here that the sending down of iron is also important for this universe.

It is said "He sent down iron."

﴿In which is severe might﴾ (57:25): for example, within iron itself lie both war and peace.

﴿And benefits for mankind﴾ (57:25): until today human civilisation and culture exist by the blessing of iron.

And then:

﴿And that Allah may know who helps Him and His Messengers in the unseen﴾ (57:25): this is a reference to jihad and fighting. It is mentioned here because jihad with wealth and jihad with one's self cannot be completed without weapons.

What is said here, that Allah wishes to make manifest those who help Allah and His Messengers in the unseen, is explained as to what the support of Allah and of the Messenger of Allah means: it refers to those who help the call and system of Allah. As far as the Being of Allah, the Exalted, is concerned, He is...

﴿Indeed Allah is Strong and Mighty﴾ (57:25). Here it has been said that prophethood is one in its reality, its Book and its call, and that the balance and the law of the Messengers is also one. Now it is explained that the Messengers too are one: they are from the descendants of Noah and Abraham.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 26:

ولقد .................... والکتب (75 : 62)
"And We sent Noah and Abraham, and placed in their offspring prophethood and the Scripture." The prophets form a single genealogical tree, whose branches are joined to one root. This tree has run since the very beginning of humanity: from Noah (ʿalayhi al-salam), then from Abraham (ʿalayhi al-salam), and after them, as humans spread, the messengerships also spread.

But the generations in which this prophethood and Scripture continued were not all alike.

فمنھم .................... فسقون (64 : 62)
"Among their offspring were some who were guided, and many of them were defiant transgressors." This is a very brief comment upon the long span of human history.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 27:

And the last link in this long history, before the Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), was this:

ثم قفینا ................ ابن مریم (75 : 72) "Then We sent, in succession, Our messengers, and after them We sent Jesus, son of Mary." That is, among the descendants of Noah and Abraham, messengers were sent one after another, and the last of them in the line was Jesus, son of Mary. Here the distinguishing characteristic of the followers of Jesus is also described.

وجعلنا .................... ورحمة (75 : 72) "And We placed in the hearts of those who followed him compassion and mercy." This compassion and mercy was the result of the call of Jesus (peace be upon him), because he laid stress on the spiritual training of people. And it is evident that through spiritual training and spiritual purification, compassion and mercy awaken. Those people who truly followed the teachings of Jesus (peace be upon him) were compassionate. Elsewhere in the Qur'an too, this quality of the Christians is alluded to. The attitude of the Christians of the early period, such as the Negus (al-Najashi) and the people of the delegation of Najran, towards Islam was also sympathetic. And in the same way, various other individuals among them came to the Abode of Islam and accepted Islam, as long as they remained among the true followers of Jesus (peace be upon him).

The Qur'an here also mentions another characteristic of the followers of the Messiah (peace be upon him), but it also makes a beautiful criticism of it.

ورھبانیة .................... رضوان اللہ (75 : 72) "And monasticism they invented themselves; We did not prescribe it for them, but they devised it seeking the pleasure of Allah." The preferred interpretation is that the monasticism seen in the history of Christianity was adopted by some followers of the Messiah, and they adopted it seeking the pleasure of Allah. They adopted it to keep away from the defilements of life. Allah had not made it obligatory for them. But when they adopted it, and made it binding upon themselves, then it was their duty to fulfil its due right, and to fulfil the requirements of purity, elevation, chastity, contentment, and remembrance and reflection which it entailed. Because they had invented it for the pleasure of God.

But what happened was that this monasticism became a mere custom, emptied of its substance. People made it a profession, and it became emptied of its true spirit. Except for a few monks, no one fulfilled its due right.

فما رعوھا ................ فسقون (75 : 72) "And they did not observe it with its due observance. So We gave those among them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient." The law of Allah is not to judge people by looking at their outward appearances, nor to look at customs and traditions. Allah looks at people's intentions and looks at their deeds; He decides on the basis of intention and action, and no one's intention is hidden from Him. He knows the secrets of hearts.

Now the final call is addressed to those who have believed, who are the last link in the history of religion and prophethood and of the Muslim nation, and who have to bear the burden of the call of the prophets until the Day of Resurrection.

O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger (ﷺ); He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will appoint for you a light by which you will walk, and will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. [So that] the People of the Book may know that they have no control over any of the bounty of Allah, and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

This is an address to the believers. It is addressed to them by their beloved name.

"O you who have believed" (Ya ayyuha alladhina amanu) — this is the voice of their hearts, a voice that settles upon the heart and revives faith. It is a reminder that they should fulfil the right of faith, and that their relationship with their Lord, who is calling them, is a relationship of faith. Therefore He addresses them by this name. Through faith, Allah calls them to fear Him and to believe in the Messenger. It appears that the "right of faith" here means a particular meaning: that they should generate the reality of faith and its effects within themselves.

"Fear Allah and believe in His Messenger (ﷺ); He will give you a double portion of His mercy" — this too is a remarkable manner of expression. The mercy of Allah cannot be divided into parts; whoever receives it receives it completely. Where would it be broken into pieces? Rather, the speech here is in accordance with the limited human mind, that you will receive two portions.

"And He will appoint for you a light by which you will walk" — this is the divine gift given to those who fear Allah and also believe in the Messenger. By this bounty hearts become soft, and they see the true reality from behind the veils. Therefore they walk straight on their path and do not go astray.

"And He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful" — in any case, a human being is human, and whatever degree of light he attains, he may still commit error. He is always in need of forgiveness, and Allah is Ghafur and Rahim.

O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger, so that you may receive a double portion of Allah's mercy, that this light may be given to you by which you traverse the journey of life, and that Allah's mercy and forgiveness may encompass you and your faults be pardoned.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 57, verse 29:

"That the People of the Book may know that they have no control over the bounty of Allah, and that the bounty is in the hand of Allah, He gives it to whomever He wills" (57:29, partial). The People of the Book held the conceit that they were the chosen people of Allah, and that they were the sons and beloved ones of Allah.

"They say: Become Jews or Christians, and you will be guided" (2:135). So Allah Almighty invites the believers to become worthy of His mercy, His Paradise, His forgiveness and His favours, and He will shower these things upon you, so that the People of the Book will know that they are caught in a false assumption, and that nothing is in their control. The bounty is in the hand of Allah, and it has come upon the Muslims. It has not been handed over to anyone's monopoly, nor has it been restricted.

"And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty" (57:29, partial).

In short, this is a call in which the Muslims were invited to compete: that you should advance in piety, purity and righteousness. This Surah concludes on this note, and the conclusion and the beginning of the Surah join together, because throughout this entire Surah there is the call "O you who believe": submit with humility before your Lord, carry out the commands of your Lord, and fulfil your financial, physical and spiritual obligations.

The manner in which the Qur'an addresses the human heart, this Surah is its finest example. Human beings are roused to good deeds with great effect. The beginning, the end and the context of this Surah all urge people toward righteous action. Its imagery, atmosphere and impact are worth witnessing, and there are lessons in it for those engaged in the work of Islamic da'wah. In it are indications of how people should be addressed and in what manner they should be stirred........ This is the teaching of Allah, who created our hearts and who is the Creator of everything. Those who call to the faith should go forth having learned from this divine school, so that their call may succeed.
